response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, forbidden-scope entry, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, stable termination, and bounded-response obligations across the closed FCSTM for case 0054's train state machine. The FCSTM shows InMotion is a wrapper composite whose exit transitions (Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken={7,8}) route to outer InMotion -> Stopping/EmergencyStopping guarded transitions (R45RouteToken==7/8). Stopping and EmergencyStopping are reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, deadlock:refuted in verify_facts), matching NL contracts NL-CONTRACT-REF-003 and NL-CONTRACT-REF-004's endpoints (both satisfied as edges exist: InMotion->Stopping via route-token 7, InMotion->EmergencyStopping via route-token 8). The obstacle-detected event (NL-CONTRACT-REF-020, event_consumer_coverage) is declared and reachably consumed from Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching (transition:line:23/24/25), satisfying reachable coverage inside InMotion. NL9's "continues to approach the destination" (NL-CONTRACT-REF-018, state_action must_progress) and NL10's state_retention (NL-CONTRACT-REF-019, must_remain until ready to stop/decelerate) both describe Approaching's obligation to persist/continue an activity, but the closed FCSTM shows Approaching has outgoing transitions (to [*] via Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, to [*] via _obstacle_detected) with no explicit continuous self-loop/do-activity distinct from the abstract 'Send' action, and no explicit readiness guard on either exit; these are preserved as predicate-null W1 per the registry (no S4-eligible phase for NL9's continuous activity, and no registered predicate for state_retention). EmergencyStopping and Stopping are genuine dead-ends (leaf, no outgoing, reachable, non-final in NL's operational sense) which could implicate deadlock_freedom, but no NL contract in this closure establishes an explicit progress/response obligation for Stopping or EmergencyStopping as an operating continuation state (EmergencyStopping's contracts are state_action/effect only, not deadlock/progress), so no V1 candidate is derived from NL-CONTRACT-REF-006/007 alone; however EmergencyStopping's action/effect (Emergency Stop, Obstacle Detected signal) map to during-abstract EmergencyStop/SendObstacleDetected placeholders with no explicit content, which is an action/effect gap, not a deadlock gap. Root reachability, owner entries (DoorsClosing, InMotion, Accelerating default entry) are all confirmed reachable_from_initial=true with proved verify facts, so no reachability/initial_entry defect exists from this lens. No forbidden-scope entry or cross-wrapper isolation issue is found since InMotion's exit-token pattern successfully routes to both Stopping and EmergencyStopping.

arguments.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, forbidden-scope entry, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, stable termination, and bounded-response obligations across the closed FCSTM for case 0054's train state machine. The FCSTM shows InMotion is a wrapper composite whose exit transitions (Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken={7,8}) route to outer InMotion -> Stopping/EmergencyStopping guarded transitions (R45RouteToken==7/8). Stopping and EmergencyStopping are reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, deadlock:refuted in verify_facts), matching NL contracts NL-CONTRACT-REF-003 and NL-CONTRACT-REF-004's endpoints (both satisfied as edges exist: InMotion->Stopping via route-token 7, InMotion->EmergencyStopping via route-token 8). The obstacle-detected event (NL-CONTRACT-REF-020, event_consumer_coverage) is declared and reachably consumed from Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching (transition:line:23/24/25), satisfying reachable coverage inside InMotion. NL9's "continues to approach the destination" (NL-CONTRACT-REF-018, state_action must_progress) and NL10's state_retention (NL-CONTRACT-REF-019, must_remain until ready to stop/decelerate) both describe Approaching's obligation to persist/continue an activity, but the closed FCSTM shows Approaching has outgoing transitions (to [*] via Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, to [*] via _obstacle_detected) with no explicit continuous self-loop/do-activity distinct from the abstract 'Send' action, and no explicit readiness guard on either exit; these are preserved as predicate-null W1 per the registry (no S4-eligible phase for NL9's continuous activity, and no registered predicate for state_retention). EmergencyStopping and Stopping are genuine dead-ends (leaf, no outgoing, reachable, non-final in NL's operational sense) which could implicate deadlock_freedom, but no NL contract in this closure establishes an explicit progress/response obligation for Stopping or EmergencyStopping as an operating continuation state (EmergencyStopping's contracts are state_action/effect only, not deadlock/progress), so no V1 candidate is derived from NL-CONTRACT-REF-006/007 alone; however EmergencyStopping's action/effect (Emergency Stop, Obstacle Detected signal) map to during-abstract EmergencyStop/SendObstacleDetected placeholders with no explicit content, which is an action/effect gap, not a deadlock gap. Root reachability, owner entries (DoorsClosing, InMotion, Accelerating default entry) are all confirmed reachable_from_initial=true with proved verify facts, so no reachability/initial_entry defect exists from this lens. No forbidden-scope entry or cross-wrapper isolation issue is found since InMotion's exit-token pattern successfully routes to both Stopping and EmergencyStopping.

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text EmergencyStopping block ('during abstract EmergencyStop;' and 'during abstract SendObstacleDetected;'); inspection_equivalent_facts.states EmergencyStopping (no outgoing transitions, is_composite=false); NL3 quote 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal'; contract NL-CONTRACT-NL3-EFFECT-1 property=effect.

issues.observed: The closed FCSTM declares EmergencyStopping with two abstract lifecycle carriers, 'during abstract EmergencyStop' and 'during abstract SendObstacleDetected'; both are opaque abstract action stubs with no send-event/effect construct, no outgoing transition from EmergencyStopping carries an effect emitting a signal, and no event named 'Obstacle Detected' appears anywhere in the model's declared event list (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, Closed_SendDeparted, Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, _obstacle_detected).
issues.reason: The NL contract requires an effect property (sending a named signal), which is a distinct semantic property from a lifecycle action per the frozen property vocabulary. issues.strongest_rebuttal: The abstract action 'SendObstacleDetected' is named to represent the same intended behavior and may be functionally equivalent to sending the signal even though the closed model represents it as an opaque action rather than a formal effect/event-emission construct; the frozen predicate registry has no expressible form for verifying an abstract action body performs a signal emission.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping lacks a signal-send effect for Obstacle Detected
